properties.description:
A low in the Gulf of Alaska will will bring a front to the Alaska
Range and Central Interior Tuesday and Wednesday. There is
uncertainty with the exact strength and placement of this front
and we are currently expecting around 3 to 6 inches of snow from
the Western Alaska Range to Fairbanks. However, there is a 30%
chance for snow accumulations exceeding 6 inches in this area.
Currently, the greatest likelihood of this occurring is towards
Eielson AFB and areas east, where Winter Storm Watches are in
effect. If the front is a bit farther to the west, this chance
increases dramatically in/around Fairbanks.

There may end up being a west to east gradient where Eielson gets
6 inches or more of snow, and Fairbanks south/west only gets a
couple of inches. We will be monitoring this storm very closely
and will have more information as the details become clearer.

Peninsula, Brazoria County beaches, Galveston Island and the
Bolivar Peninsula.

* WHEN...Through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away

current. If able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If
unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Glacier Bay; City and Borough of Juneau
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 17 at 2:08PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
ESFAJK

A strong storm system is expected to move over the northern Alaska
Panhandle beginning Monday night and continuing through Tuesday.
Juneau and Gustavus are expected to see periods of moderate to heavy
rain for a majority of the day on Tuesday, resulting in significant
and rapid rises on small creeks and streams. Rain totals for this
event are around 2-4 inches over a 36 hour period, though expected
totals will likely change as the event moves closer. At this time,
expect to see similar impacts to the previous storm system we saw on
Friday, where Salmon River, Jordan Creek, and Montana Creek reached
either near or into minor flood stage. Additionally, ponding of water
on roads and areas of poor drainage is possible.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to assess the
situation and make updates to the forecast.
